presentation: Chaptered implementation/evidence guide, not continuous live screen recording
voice: Windows System.Speech synthetic narration; no person impersonated

scenes.title: Problem: developing failures in essential services
scenes.narration: We are RASCALS from Hindustan Institute of Technology and Science. ContinuityGuard identifies developing system faults and gives operators a reviewable warning before disruption. Our demonstration uses original controlled scenarios, with a separate experiment containing actual LinuxONE service measurements. This is a chaptered evidence walkthrough, with labeled synthetic narration.

scenes.title: Solution: AI and the decision path stay on LinuxONE
scenes.narration: Native s390x Jupyter fits and tests the models. The deployed app combines calibrated boosted-tree forecasts, a threshold guard and separate novelty scores. Persistent signals create incidents with retained measurements, dependency priorities and runbooks. Local Granite generates constrained wording. The operator can inspect a paired simulator response before deciding what to investigate.

scenes.title: Working scenarios and actual operator output
scenes.narration: The actual dashboard runs on the assigned IBM VM. Pool pressure and retry-cascade examples warn before sustained service breach. A sudden failure is detected at onset, without a promised precursor. The action preview reports modeled benefit with deferred optional work. It executes no remediation against a real service.

scenes.title: Original measurements, with raw-data provenance
scenes.narration: We also collected real request timings and process counters from a bounded microservice on LinuxONE. Increased request computation raised measured latency. A separate baseline-trained novelty detector flagged the controlled pressure. The raw CSV, timestamps, recovery false alerts and hash are published. This experiment does not validate hospital outage prediction.

scenes.title: Evaluation: report the misses and competitive baseline
scenes.narration: On sixty fresh synthetic runs, both ContinuityGuard and static thresholds warned before thirty-one of forty-three service incidents. Median early lead was thirteen seconds versus ten. Precision was fifty-nine point three percent versus sixty percent. These results and uncertainty do not establish consistent model superiority. Earlier development reports remain available.

scenes.title: LinuxONE proof, tests and IBM Toolkit boundary
scenes.narration: 37 native tests passed. Actual authenticated HTTP ingestion processed all one thousand offered events in the short test. Container controls, model hashes and restart evidence are public. IBM Toolkit deployment guidance was applied, and an optional Random Forest export was checked. Entitled Toolkit execution and hardware acceleration are not claimed.

scenes.title: Learnings and a complete reproducible handoff
scenes.narration: We learned to align prediction and evaluation horizons, distinguish queue timing from inference, and separate measured data from simulation. The repository contains the summary, five executed notebooks, scenarios, source, outputs, deployment and access instructions. Review the short video, confirm required labs and submit manually. ContinuityGuard makes warning evidence and next steps inspectable.
